rfm_tuples.R: "On August 5, 2025, the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger ... with MasterBrand, Inc ... at the effective time of the Merger, each share of Company common stock outstanding ... will be automatically converted into the right to receive 5.15 shares of MasterBrand common stock." Issuer also discloses receipt of an FTC Second Request.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the fact of the merger and the exchange ratio in EDGAR; Mode B — assess the implied near-term outcome distribution given (a) FTC Second Request issuance, (b) -44% drawdown reflecting widening merger-arb spread, (c) Q3 FY26 goodwill impairment triggered by sustained stock-price decline.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q Note 1 merger disclosure + risk factors) and edgar_fts (Form 8-K calendar)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Merger announced 2025-08-05 (8-K filing). Fixed-exchange-ratio: 1 AMWD = 5.15 MasterBrand shares. MasterBrand legacy holders end up with ~63% of combined company. Both parties received FTC Second Request — disclosure language: 'continue to work cooperatively with the FTC to obtain regulatory clearance as expeditiously as possible.' AMWD recorded $30.1M goodwill impairment in Q3 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-01-31) — the issuer explicitly states the impairment trigger was 'a sustained decline in our stock price ... and changes to the implied consideration of the Merger transaction.' Q3 FY26 alone: $324M revenue (-18.4% YoY), $28.7M net loss, plus $4M of Merger-related expenses. Nine-month FY26: $1.12B revenue (-14.3% YoY), $8.0M net LOSS vs $73.9M net income prior. Issuer has paused share repurchases pending Merger close.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the dominant macro context for the drawdown. The -44% drop is NOT primarily an operational distress signal — it is (a) deteriorating standalone fundamentals (-14% YoY sales, swing to net loss, $30M goodwill writedown) compounded by (b) merger-arb spread widening on FTC Second Request risk and (c) MasterBrand share-price decline (since deal is fixed-ratio stock-for-stock, AMWD tracks 5.15x MBC). Disclosure is honest and comprehensive. Severity moderate because: the issuer flagged stock-price decline as the impairment trigger transparently, and the merger pathway provides a defined floor (5.15x MBC) absent FTC block.

rfm_tuples.R: "Net sales for fiscal 2025 decreased 7.5% to $1,709.6 million from the prior fiscal year. Sales in the home center channel decreased 9.3% and the independent dealer and distributor channel decreased 8.9% ... new construction channel ... decreased 5.1%, primarily due to weaker housing completions throughout the second half of the fiscal year, as home builders continue to be impacted by high mortgage rates, weaker consumer confidence, and government policy related uncertainty."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the FY2025 disclosure against the Q3 FY26 (period ending 2026-01-31) actuals to check whether the deterioration accelerated or stabilized after the 10-K was filed.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2025 (yr ended 2025-04-30): Net sales $1,709.6M (-7.5%), gross profit 17.9% (down from 20.4%), net income $99.5M (down $16.8M from $116M), all three channels declining. Forward to first 9 months of FY26 (period ending 2026-01-31): Net sales $1,122M (-14.3% YoY vs prior 9-mo $1,309M), nine-month NET LOSS of $8.0M vs net income $73.9M prior — i.e., the trajectory ACCELERATED downward, not stabilized. Q3 FY26 stand-alone net sales $324.3M vs $397.6M (-18.4%). Goodwill impairment $30.1M booked Q3. Customer concentration unchanged: Home Depot + Lowe's still ~40% combined (Q3 FY26 Customer A = 37%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The deterioration accelerated from -7.5% FY25 to -18.4% Q3 FY26 YoY. The business is in a genuine cyclical/structural downturn — high mortgage rates persisting, existing-home-sales at thirty-year lows, two-customer concentration of ~40% with no contractual offset. Severe because the issuer's narrative implicitly anchors on macro recovery that has NOT materialized, AND the Q3 swing to GAAP net loss is a meaningful break in trend. Combined with insider Form 4 pattern (no buying into the decline), this is the strongest standalone-fundamentals red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: "During the third quarter of fiscal 2026, the Company concluded that a goodwill impairment indicator existed due to a sustained decline in our stock price, which could more likely than not result in the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeding the fair value ... goodwill impairment analysis as of December 31, 2025 indicated a goodwill impairment of $30 [million]."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given stock-price-triggered impairment of $30M, assess remaining goodwill-at-risk and the implication for FY26 GAAP profitability if drawdown deepens.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $30.1M goodwill impairment booked Q3 FY26 — issuer explicitly attributes the trigger to 'sustained decline in our stock price' and 'changes to the implied consideration of the Merger transaction.' Goodwill fair-value test used Level 2 inputs (i.e., implied merger consideration referenced market price of MBC). Issuer notes that further stock-price decline could trigger additional impairment in future quarters.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure — issuer states the trigger plainly and explains the Level 2 input methodology tying impairment math to merger-implied price. This is a non-cash charge but it (a) signals that internal valuation models are now anchored to the merger-implied price rather than DCF / standalone fundamentals, and (b) creates additional GAAP-loss headwind in Q4 FY26 if MBC continues to decline. Not severe (cash flows unaffected) but a confirmation that fundamentals + market price are both pointing the same direction.

Adjusted EBITDA is the operative measure for the Term Loan covenants. With net sales down ~14% YoY 9-mo and $30M goodwill impairment, GAAP earnings are negative YTD — meaning the Adjusted EBITDA add-backs (goodwill impairment, merger-related expenses) are doing meaningful work to keep covenant compliance. Issuer asserts compliance and does NOT disclose a going-concern paragraph or a waiver/amendment. Cash $48.2M FY25 (down from $87.4M prior).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B gap: issuer asserts compliance but does not disclose actual covenant cushion. The covenant package (4.0x net leverage, 2.0x interest coverage) is relatively generous and unlikely binding at current ~$370M debt + Adjusted-EBITDA add-backs that include the $30M goodwill charge. Cash drained from $87M to $48M YoY = -45%, partly from $96.7M of FY25 buybacks now suspended. No going-concern flag. Mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS because the specific ratios were not disclosed.

Tariffs on imported cabinets/vanities benefit AMWD relative to Chinese competitors (AMWD manufactures domestically), but the company also imports certain components. Net: visible margin damage, transparent narrative, no Mode-B gap.

rfm_tuples.M_value: FY25 Home Depot + Lowe's combined ~40% of net sales. Q3 FY26 Customer A = 37% of net sales (single customer over 30% threshold, no contractual long-term agreement). MasterBrand is also a Top-3 cabinet supplier to Home Depot and Lowe's — the combined AMWD+MBC would likely be the dominant cabinet vendor to BOTH big-box retailers. This is plausibly the FTC's antitrust concern triggering the Second Request: vertical squeeze on home-center cabinet category.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: customer concentration plus pending merger to another cabinet maker with overlapping channels = structural antitrust risk. The 10-K discloses customer concentration but does NOT frame this dimension of the Merger antitrust risk (left to the M&A risk factors). Combined entity dominance in two big-box channels is the likely FTC theory. Non-fatal — divestitures or behavioral remedies could clear — but it explains why merger-arb spread is wide.

rfm_tuples.R: Critical Audit Matter (Ernst & Young, auditor since 2022): "Timing of Revenue Recognition ... where title transfer takes place upon delivery to the customer's location, the Company must estimate the amount of sales for products that have been shipped but not yet delivered. This estimate of sales shipped but not delivered is calculated using a lag factor ... Auditing management's lag factor estimate was complex due to the significant judgments made by management in determining the length of time to be used in calculating the estimated days between shipment and delivery date."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — assess judgment-area risk and whether period-end shipment cut-offs are a chronic earnings-management lever, particularly into a declining-sales trend.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CAM is revenue-cutoff judgment around shipped-but-not-yet-delivered orders. EY auditor since 2022 (no auditor change). Clean opinion. Lag-factor methodology is management-determined and the CAM language explicitly flags 'Management's selected time period as opposed to a longer, shorter, or more recent period of time could have a significant effect on the amount of sales recorded as of period end.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CAM is on a real judgment area (period-end revenue cutoff) — auditor flagging this in a -14% revenue trend year deserves note. No restatement, no auditor change, no material weakness — but the existence of the CAM means the auditor specifically called out that management's estimate could swing reported sales materially. Watch for any restatement risk or 10-K/A amendment post-Merger. Mild Mode-B flag.

summary: AMWD is a -44.1% drawdown name dominated by a single contextual fact: AMWD is in a pending fixed-ratio stock-for-stock merger with MasterBrand (announced 2025-08-05, exchange ratio 5.15 MBC per AMWD share) currently under FTC Second Request. The drawdown reflects (a) merger-arb spread widening on antitrust risk, (b) MBC's own stock decline (since deal is fixed-ratio), and (c) genuine standalone-fundamentals deterioration: FY25 net sales -7.5%, accelerating to Q3 FY26 -18.4% YoY with a swing to $28.7M GAAP net loss, plus $30M goodwill impairment whose trigger the issuer explicitly attributes to sustained stock-price decline. Forensic Form-4 read is mixed: ZERO open-market purchases by any insider in the 12 months pre-cutoff (only one $52K director buy in 24 months, pre-merger) — but absence-of-buying is confounded by M&A blackout restrictions. STRONGER forensic finding: CEO M. Scott Culbreth + insider James G. Davis sold COMBINED $1.43M of open-market stock in Oct-Dec 2024 at $80-93 (avg $87) — eight months before the Merger was announced — stock subsequently fell ~50% from those prices. Clustered pre-bad-news selling by two execs with zero offsetting buys is the cleanest Mode-B red flag. Disclosure quality is high (no auditor change, clean E&Y opinion, transparent goodwill-impairment trigger, full Merger risk factors, customer-concentration acknowledged). Severity counts: 1 PASS / 1 UNVERIFIABLE / 6 MODERATE / 1 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG. Verdict: NEUTRAL leaning SHORT-tier — fundamentals are genuinely impaired and pre-merger insider selling is asymmetric, BUT the fixed-ratio merger to MBC provides a defined consideration floor (5.15x MBC, regulatory closing risk notwithstanding), which prevents this from being a pure SHORT setup. The cleanest interpretation: the value of AMWD at cutoff IS 5.15 × MBC × P(close) + standalone-AMWD × P(break) — i.e., this is a merger-arb position, not a standalone forensic call.
